professionalSummary: Developed and maintained the alert queue and case views of the compliance web application using TypeScript and Angular, implementing server‑side paging and column virtualisation to replace full‑queue downloads.
Owned the component (Jest) and end‑to‑end (Cypress) test suites, keeping them passing in the CI pipeline and adding a queue‑load smoke test that gates releases.
Reduced median alert‑queue load time from 6.2 s to 1.4 s over four weeks, measured by real‑user monitoring against the published baseline.
Coordinated API changes with the backend team, adapting views to paged endpoints after approval in the API review.
Authored release notes documenting known limitations and hand‑over conditions for each application release.
experienceHighlights: Alert queue and case views development and maintenance (TypeScript, Angular).
Component and end‑to‑end test suite ownership (Jest, Cypress).
Performance improvement: median load time 6.2 s → 1.4 s, real‑user monitoring over four weeks.
API coordination with backend team, including approval and adaptation to paged endpoints.
Release documentation: known limitations and hand‑over notes.
projectsAndWorkSamples: Real‑user monitoring export of median queue load time per day for eight weeks, baseline line, paging release marker (src_8b9385dd5087).
Cypress smoke test with pipeline run identifiers (src_8b9385dd5087).

evidence.text: Owned the component test suite (Jest) and the end-to-end suite (Cypress) for the application, keeping both passing in the pipeline and adding a queue-load smoke test that gates releases.

Median alert-queue load time for analysts fell from 6.2 seconds to 1.4 seconds after the paging release, measured by the application's real-user monitoring over the following four weeks against the published baseline of 6.2 seconds.
Coordinated API changes with the backend team in the API review; the backend lead approved endpoint changes and I adapted the views to the paged endpoints.

Wrote the release notes for each application release, including the known limitation that column sorting was applied per page rather than across the whole queue, and the hand-over notes for the frontend on-call.
